sections.title: Intro
points: 1.0 drops 11 December - before it does, every PoE 2 league so far, ranked.
Two years of Early Access: the launch, four challenge leagues and an event league.
Hook: tease the most controversial placement before revealing anything.

sections.title: How I'm ranking them
points: The league mechanic itself - fun to engage with, not just profitable.
Loot and economy - did it feel rewarding, could you progress.
The patch around it - balance, endgame, how the game felt that season.
Staying power - did people keep playing, did it get better or fall off.
Worth saying: every one of these mechanics is now core, so you're ranking stuff that's still in your game.
prompts: Your own background: played since the 0.1 launch, did the 0.1 subathon.
deeper: 0.1 subathon was one minute per sub until Christmas.
There was a GhazzyTV meetup after the 0.1 subathon.

sections.title: 0.1 - Early Access launch
sections.subtitle: 6 December 2024 - no challenge league
points: No challenge league - everyone was on Early Access Standard. Rank it as a league or as 'the launch'?
What we had: 3 acts (plus Cruel), 6 classes, ~50 areas, ~175 skills.
The hype: over a million Early Access copies sold.
Your Demon Magus wish started here - 'screaming for it since 0.1'.
prompts: Was 0.1 the most fun you had despite being the least finished?
What did 0.1 get right that later patches lost?
deeper: 1.0 is roughly 3x faster on CPU than 0.1.0, per the keynote.

sections.title: 0.2 - Dawn of the Hunt
sections.subtitle: 4 April - 26 August 2025
points: First seasonal league - but officially not a 'full league': everything shipped straight into core, nothing exclusive.
Azmerian Wisps - they flee, you chase, monsters they touch get stronger and more rewarding.
12 Rogue Exiles that use and drop their own uniques, plus 4 unique Strongboxes.
The Huntress (Amazon, Ritualist) and spears; new Smith of Kitava, Tactician and Lich ascendancies.
100+ new uniques, 100+ new supports, 8 new endgame maps.
prompts: Does a league without a real mechanic even deserve a tier?
Huntress / spear launch - how did the class feel?

sections.title: 0.3 - Rise of the Abyssal
sections.subtitle: The Third Edict - 29 August - 9 December 2025
points: PoE 2's first proper 'full league'.
Fissures near packs - kill them, Abyssals climb out with necromantic mods, close the Abyss for a trove; sometimes it opens the Abyssal Depths.
Bones and the Well of Souls: hidden Desecrated mods, reveal and pick one of three. Also juiced waystones.
The patch was massive: Act 4 (non-linear, eight islands), Cruel removed for three interludes to 65.
Plus a support gem overhaul, an essence rework and a full balance pass.
prompts: Was desecration the best crafting addition PoE 2 has had?
Shortest league of the lot - did it end too early or at the right time?
deeper: Abyss went core in 0.4 and got its own Atlas passive tree.
Abyssal Lich alternate ascendancy came with the Abyss mechanic.

sections.title: 0.4 - Fate of the Vaal
sections.subtitle: The Last of the Druids - 12 December 2025 - 25 May 2026
points: Vaal structures across Wraeclast - sacrifice nearby monsters to power devices that take you to Atziri's Temple.
You build the temple yourself - pick rooms, place them next to rooms that level them up; Royal Architect and Atziri at the top.
Vaal crafting: corruption benches, Architect's Orb, Vaal Cultivation Orb, transcendent limbs.
The Druid (Oracle, Shaman) and Talismans - shapeshifting into animal forms.
Tavern Talk take: big drop-off early over the economy, then the temple endgame won back the people who stayed.
prompts: Agree with that take - slow start, great endgame?
Longest league of the lot - earned it or overstayed?
deeper: 250+ new passives and the first Lineage Supports (8+).

sections.title: 0.5 - Runes of Aldur
sections.subtitle: Return of the Ancients - 29 May 2026 - early December 2026
points: A Remnant in every area - slot runeshapes to pick the item you want, then fight waves of risen monsters for it.
More runes = more waves and harder mods, but better items; Remnants roll 2-10 slots.
Verisium and Runeforging - and Runic Ward, a defence that kicks in at 1 life.
Runeforging also upgrades low-level uniques so they stay usable late.
Shipped with the 'Origins of Divinity' endgame overhaul - Delirium, Breach, Ritual and Expedition all reworked.
prompts: Deterministic crafting - did it make loot feel worse or better?
Runic Ward - did it change how you built characters?
deeper: 23 Kalguuran skills, 13 Alloys, Fluxes, Ancient and Mythical runes all come out of Remnants.
Moved to core in 0.5.5; still running until just before 1.0.

sections.title: Bonus: 0.5.5 - Forbidden Rites (event league)
sections.subtitle: 4 September 2026 - runs alongside Runes of Aldur
points: Event league - Ritual in every campaign area, with levelling rewards instead of endgame ones.
Boss rituals chain: beat the boss and it carries into the next ritual's waves; spend the tribute on uniques.
Sacred Blooms bring back the Viridian Wildwood and wisps on your Atlas.
Trial of Chaos finally lets you leave mid-run.
prompts: Does an event league get a tier, or does it sit off the board?
deeper: You were playing it late October - Ritual and Delirium Atlas points.

sections.title: The full board - and what 1.0 needs to learn
points: Reveal the final board; call out the biggest gap between tiers.
1.0 league is Conquerors of Wraeclast - troops, castles, sieges, three factions, 100 castles on one shared Atlas.
Your ExileCon reaction: 'straight up my alley' - RTS and risk woven into PoE.
Your 1.0 start: Infernalist, triple Hellhounds / Demon Magus - then Shadow.
prompts: Which past mechanic should 1.0 learn the most from?
Where would Conquerors land if it plays like the keynote?
deeper: 1.0 also adds Acts 5-6, the Shadow and Duelist, ~110 effectively new uniques, a 70-node Atlas tree.

sections.title: Outro
points: Ask: where would you put each league - drop your tier list in the comments.
Plug the 1.0 launch subathon.
